actual.affected_use: 1.1 **Input and framing convention.** Let h be one four-dimensional one-handle with feet in a connected compact oriented three-dimensional base N. Let B and B′ be two embedded replacement arcs joining its feet, with framed product tubes and the same parametrized germs at their endpoints. They avoid every other one-handle foot and the protected boundary collar. A finite system of framed two-handle attaching curves may traverse h any number of times, with either orientation. Apply the explicit cancellation/routing construction with either arc. Its links are $R_B(L)\cup U\qquad\hbox{and}\qquad R_{B'}(L)\cup U.$ Here U may be chosen as the same small zero-framed circle in both diagrams: take its cross-section on the common endpoint germ. Its disk meets each routed strip once for each signed traversal of h. Its framing is the product disk framing. This convention follows by transporting the meridian along the product cancellation tube; it fixes the actual exterior marking. Assume first that B and B′ have disjoint interiors outside their common endpoint germs. No restriction is placed on the homotopy class of their union. The two framed arc strips, with oppositely oriented common germs, join to a framed embedded ribbon annulus about a closed curve K that follows B′ and returns along a parallel of B. More precisely separate the strips by distinct normal coordinates, cut both just inside their common germs, and join the four short ends by the two planar rectangles in the endpoint balls. The core of the resulting annulus is K. Its annular normal is the integer framing used below. This choice records any difference in twisting of the two replacement arc framings; no independently chosen integer is substituted. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, construct]
actual.reason: The Statement specifies only an oriented three-dimensional base, not an oriented four-dimensional attachment. A twisted one-handle can make the closed core normal bundle nonorientable, so F2 cannot supply the framed surgery pair. Require an oriented stage / orientation-compatible attachment, or explicitly require a closed-core product framing. This is outside the assigned item scope.
